synthesis: DEV-2460 is the scaffolding ticket for the 9-card Company Metrics epic (DEV-2409). No new metric. Four changes: (1) reorder CompanyMetricsOverview::cards() from its append-grown 8 keys to 7 in mockup-relative order, dropping kit-users, with a docblock that records the 9 empty slots as load-bearing so siblings drop in without a second reorder; (2) relabel RecoveryCounts -> 'Total Repossessions' and RecoveryLeader -> 'LPR Recovery Leaderboard'; (3) move Active Kit Users out of the grid into HotlistCount's header row at position 5 of 6, reusing KitUsers' existing cached methods by composition; (4) introduce a canViewCardData()/lockedStat()/expandableCards() Pro-gate seam that gates NO real card yet -- it only establishes the contract 9 siblings will code against. The prior full attempt (claude/DEV-2409, PR #369) reached 4,000+ lines across 28 files over 8 adversarial review rounds and never cleared the >=90 gate, each round finding an unrepaired sibling of the previous fix. This ticket is deliberately small and its dominant risk is the same one: a missed sibling call site.

Do NOT add key validation to Dashboard::toggleCard(). It has none today and needs none: expandedCardComponents() already does `cardWidgets()[$key] ?? null` and returns [] on a miss, so an unknown/locked key is already a structural no-op. Adding an `if (! isset(...)) return;` guard introduces a bug -- the early return fires before the close branch, so a card open when it becomes locked can never be closed. lockedStat() must also emit NO wire:click, giving two independent reasons a locked card cannot expand.

AC-7 is satisfiable and testable. KitUsers' two cached queries ALREADY run today because KitUsers is currently a grid card, so relocating them to HotlistCount is net-neutral for the page. DB::listen is dead for the CH driver, so the proof is (a) a code-path audit showing no new CH call site and (b) a test asserting the two pre-existing cache keys are the ones read.

BLAST RADIUS IS NON-EMPTY. The Pro-gate seam is the mechanism every future paid card will use to hide its value. If the gate runs AFTER toStat() rather than before, Pro-only data leaks to non-Pro orgs the moment a sibling wires a real gate -- and it ships silently because nothing is gated here. Therefore getStats() must branch on canViewCardData() BEFORE calling toStat(), and review escalates to 3 lanes.

questions.q: HotlistCount goes from 5 stats to 6. Should getColumns() become a plain int 6, or responsive breakpoints? Related and load-bearing: resources/css/filament/app/theme.css sets .big-stat-chart { min-h-40 } = 160px, and its comment states that number was measured as the header row's height AT THE DEFAULT 5-COLUMN WIDTH, closing with 'Revisit here if the top row's copy changes.' This ticket changes both the copy and the column count, so that calibration is invalidated by construction.
questions.answer: Responsive breakpoints, and re-check the 160px card-height floor during QA. getColumns() becomes responsive (default 1 / sm 2 / md 3 / xl 6) rather than a flat int 6; theme.css's min-h-40 calibration comment is updated to describe the 6-column reality, and the actual visual parity is verified by eye in human QA.
questions.evidence: driver found theme.css (absent from every candidate's inventory; surfaced by the grep backstop). Candidate 1 independently reports the closed DEV-2409 branch's QA pass made getColumns() responsive (default 1 / sm 2 / md 3 / xl 6) rather than a flat 6.
questions.recommendation: Responsive, and re-check the 160px floor during QA.

questions.q: Moving Active Kit Users to a header stat REMOVES its click-to-expand table (KitUsers::table(), the list of currently-active kit names). HotlistCount's header stats have no click-to-expand chrome at all. Is losing that interactive list acceptable?
questions.answer: Accept the loss of the click-to-expand kit-name table. The mockup shows Active Kit Users as a plain header stat with no expand affordance, so this matches the design. It MUST be recorded explicitly in the PR and the Jira Build Record as a deliberate, known consequence -- not left unremarked. KitUsers.php stays in the codebase, so the table can be rehomed later if anyone misses it.
questions.evidence: candidate 1 raised it. Candidate 3 argues it is out of scope because the mockup shows Kit Users as a plain header stat with no expand affordance. The ticket text does not address it.
questions.recommendation: Accept the loss -- the mockup shows it as a plain stat -- but say so explicitly rather than letting it go unremarked.

questions.answer: Yes -- update RecoveryCounts::getDatasetLabel() to 'Total Repossessions' so the internal series name and the visible card title agree.
